controls.criterion: Per-inference resource accounting bounds consumption; guardrail cascade/rogue/insecure-relay detection (ASI08/ASI10/ASI07 lenses); TLS/mTLS on every channel the plane controls; observed access edges map the actual interconnection structure.

controls.title: Accountability risks
controls.requirement: Agentic architectures obscure what caused an action: opaque decision-making, sub-agent spawning, non-reproducibility, log volume, hallucination, and processes outpacing human monitoring.
controls.criterion: Every action is attributable in an append-only, hash-chained, integrity-verified ledger (immutable by construction); a reconstructable forensic timeline and privileged-session recordings answer 'what caused this action' after the fact.
controls.note: The guidance asks for monitoring of agent INTERNAL processes and intention-vs-behavior anomaly detection; the plane evidences action-level attribution and session replay, not model-internal introspection.

frameworks.name: CISA/NSA/FBI — AI Data Security (joint CSI)
frameworks.authority: NSA's Artificial Intelligence Security Center (AISC), CISA, FBI, ASD's ACSC, NCSC-NZ and NCSC-UK
frameworks.disclaimer: Crosswalk to the ten best practices of the joint CSI 'AI Data Security' (2025-05-22), structured over the NIST AI RMF lifecycle stages. GUIDANCE, not a certifiable standard; design-toward, no conformance claim. Practices the control plane cannot evidence (secure media sanitization, privacy-preserving computation) are honest gaps or carry explicit coverage notes.

pin.document: AI Data Security: Best Practices for Securing Data Used to Train & Operate AI Systems

controls.title: Source reliable data and track data provenance
controls.requirement: Use authoritative data sources and maintain provenance — the CSI prescribes a cryptographically signed, immutable, append-only ledger of data changes.
controls.criterion: Dataset records carry provenance attestation and are sealed into the ledger-anchored AIBOM; data-lineage rows track flow within the perimeter; the provenance anchor is the append-only, hash-chained, Ed25519-signed audit ledger — literally the construction the CSI prescribes.

controls.title: Verify and maintain data integrity during storage and transport
controls.requirement: Use checksums and cryptographic hashes to verify data has not been altered or tampered with during storage or transmission.
controls.criterion: Dataset/artifact content hashes ride in the AIBOM and admission verdicts, the ledger hash-chain verifies live, and TLS protects every transport the plane controls.

controls.title: Employ digital signatures to authenticate trusted data revisions
controls.requirement: Cryptographically sign original data and every revision; adopt quantum-resistant digital signature standards.
controls.criterion: Signed-model admission verifies artifact signatures before admission (OpenSSF Model Signing / Sigstore), and the ledger's per-event Ed25519 signatures authenticate the evidence trail.
controls.note: Quantum-resistant signatures (e.g. ML-DSA) are a tracked roadmap item (docs/SEC-G3, CNSA 2.0 milestone in the calendar), not shipped — current signing is Ed25519/ECDSA/RSA.

controls.title: Leverage trusted infrastructure
controls.requirement: Use a trusted computing environment leveraging Zero Trust architecture; provide secure enclaves for sensitive data processing.
controls.criterion: Deny-closed RBAC + fail-closed multi-tenant isolation, secure-by-default deployment posture, and TLS-by-default transport evidence the Zero-Trust slice the plane controls.
controls.note: Hardware secure enclaves / confidential computing are estate infrastructure duties the plane does not evidence.

controls.title: Classify data and use access controls
controls.requirement: Categorize data by sensitivity with a classification system; classify AI system output at the level of its input data; gate access accordingly.
controls.criterion: Deterministic sensitivity/PII classification labels governed content (named rule + count, never values), a deny-closed DLP gate keyed on those classes restricts egress, and RBAC gates access.

controls.title: Encrypt data
controls.requirement: Secure data at rest, in transit and during processing with encryption proportional to the protection level (AES-256 cited as the de facto standard; TLS or post-quantum in transit).
controls.criterion: TLS ≥1.2 (with PQC hybrid key exchange where supported, docs/SEC-G3) protects transit by default; at-rest encryption is attested per tenant (opt-in — absent until attested).
controls.note: Encryption DURING PROCESSING (confidential computing) is not evidenced by the control plane.

controls.title: Store data securely
controls.requirement: Store data in certified storage devices enforcing NIST FIPS 140-3 compliance.
controls.criterion: At-rest encryption attestation per tenant; the FIPS-mode build pins a FIPS 140-3 validated module (docs/SEC-G3) — the FIPS 140-2 sunset is a calendar milestone.
controls.note: FIPS 140-3-validated STORAGE DEVICES are an estate/hardware duty the control plane cannot evidence; the plane evidences the tenant's at-rest encryption attestation and its own FIPS-mode build only — never read this as certified-storage coverage.

controls.title: Leverage privacy-preserving techniques
controls.requirement: Apply data masking/depersonalization, differential privacy, federated learning and secure multi-party computation where practical.
controls.criterion: Structural data minimization (only relations/metadata persisted, never payloads) and deterministic PII discovery making personal data visible for reduction.
controls.note: Differential privacy, federated learning and SMPC are model/data-pipeline techniques the control plane does not implement or evidence.

controls.title: Delete data securely
controls.requirement: Erase drives with cryptographic erase, block erase or data overwrite (NIST SP 800-88) before repurposing or decommissioning.
controls.criterion: Evidence of NIST SP 800-88 media sanitization for storage used by AI data.

controls.title: Conduct ongoing data security risk assessments
controls.requirement: Conduct ongoing risk assessments using industry-standard frameworks (NIST RMF, NIST AI 100-1) to evaluate the AI data security landscape and prioritize actions.
controls.criterion: Recurring, governed AI risk classifications (EU AI Act × NIST AI RMF cross-walk), continuous threat detection and least-privilege drift provide the live assessment signal.

frameworks.name: CSA AI Controls Matrix (AICM)
frameworks.version: Cloud Security Alliance — AI Controls Matrix v1.1 (bundle 2026-06)
frameworks.authority: Cloud Security Alliance (CSA)
frameworks.disclaimer: Positioning crosswalk of control-plane capabilities to the CSA AI Controls Matrix (AICM): 247 control objectives across 18 security domains — the 17 Cloud Controls Matrix (CCM v4) domains plus the new AI-specific Model Security (MDS) domain. Coverage is mapped at the DOMAIN level: each domain lists the capabilities that honestly evidence SOME of its control objectives; it is NOT a per-objective conformance claim. Domains the control plane cannot evidence (Datacenter Security, Human Resources Security, Business Continuity, Interoperability & Portability, Universal Endpoint Management) are honest nil-capability gaps. AICM v1.1 ships with AI-CAIQ v1.1, implementation and auditing guidance, and expanded mappings to ISO 42001, EU AI Act, BSI AIC4, NIST AI RMF/AI 600-1 and AIUC-1. STAR for AI Level 1 self-assessment (AI-CAIQ v1.1 submitted to the STAR Registry) is the program level available today; certification levels are upcoming — the module signals design-toward readiness, never a certification claim. Not a certification or conformance claim.

pin.document: CSA AI Controls Matrix (AICM) v1.1 — 247 control objectives across 18 domains

controls.title: Audit and Assurance
controls.requirement: Establish, plan and execute independent audits and assessments of the AI/cloud control environment, with attestable evidence.
controls.criterion: An append-only, hash-chained audit ledger with live integrity verification and continuous WORM/SIEM export provides tamper-evident assurance evidence; per-agent risk classification feeds the audit scope.
controls.note: Evidences the audit EVIDENCE substrate; the independent-assessment program and audit scheduling are an organizational process the control plane does not run.

controls.title: Application and Interface Security
controls.requirement: Secure application and interface (API) design, including input validation, against attacks on the AI application surface.
controls.criterion: Guardrail threat detection over agent/application I/O, red-team adversarial robustness testing, TLS on every interface, and secure-by-default posture.

controls.title: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
controls.requirement: Business continuity, disaster recovery, backup and resilience planning for AI systems and their supporting infrastructure.
controls.criterion: Backup/restore, failover and BC/DR planning are estate/infrastructure duties.
controls.note: Honest gap: the control plane does not evidence backup, disaster recovery or business-continuity controls — these are estate/infrastructure responsibilities.

controls.title: Change Control and Configuration Management
controls.requirement: Govern changes and configuration of AI systems and their supporting components across the lifecycle.
controls.criterion: Governed deployment/change-ledger records, secure-by-default configuration, and a signed/SBOM-backed pinned supply chain for the platform's own components.

controls.title: Cryptography, Encryption and Key Management
controls.requirement: Apply cryptography to protect AI data and manage cryptographic keys across their lifecycle.
controls.criterion: TLS protects data in transit by default; at-rest encryption is attested per tenant (opt-in).
controls.note: Encryption in transit is by design; at-rest is opt-in (a gap until attested). Cryptographic KEY MANAGEMENT (rotation, escrow, HSM) is not evidenced by the control plane.

controls.title: Datacenter Security
controls.requirement: Physical and environmental security of the datacenters hosting AI systems.
controls.criterion: Physical/datacenter security is an estate/facilities duty.
controls.note: Honest gap: physical and datacenter security is outside the control plane's scope.

controls.title: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
controls.requirement: Govern the security and privacy of data across its lifecycle in AI systems, including classification, minimization, residency and leakage prevention.
controls.criterion: Data minimization by construction, deterministic PII/sensitivity discovery, a deny-closed DLP egress gate, data-lineage within the perimeter, and a residency attestation with no observed egress violation.

controls.title: Governance, Risk and Compliance
controls.requirement: Establish AI governance, risk management and compliance processes, with an inventory of AI systems and their risk posture.
controls.criterion: Governed, audited per-agent AI risk classifications (EU AI Act × NIST), a maintained system/agent inventory, and an append-only audit trail of governance actions.

controls.title: Human Resources Security
controls.requirement: Personnel security across hiring, employment and termination for staff operating AI systems.
controls.criterion: Personnel/HR security is an organizational process.
controls.note: Honest gap: human-resources security (background checks, onboarding/offboarding, training) is an organizational duty the control plane does not evidence.

controls.title: Identity and Access Management
controls.requirement: Manage identities (including non-human/agent identities) and enforce least-privilege access across the AI estate.
controls.criterion: Governed non-human identities and policies, engine-enforced RBAC + fail-closed isolation, observed agent→resource access edges, and permitted-vs-observed least-privilege drift.

controls.title: Interoperability and Portability
controls.requirement: Ensure data and service interoperability and portability for AI systems to avoid lock-in.
controls.criterion: Workload/data portability between providers is a deployment-architecture concern.
controls.note: Honest gap: AI workload/data portability and provider interoperability are deployment-architecture concerns; the plane's interoperable compliance-evidence export (OSCAL/CEF/syslog/OTLP) supports audit portability but is not a portability control for the customer's AI workloads.

controls.title: Infrastructure and Virtualization Security
controls.requirement: Secure the infrastructure and virtualization layer hosting AI systems, including segmentation and hardening.
controls.criterion: Secure-by-default deployment posture, TLS in transit, and RBAC + fail-closed multi-tenant isolation enforced by the engine.
controls.note: Evidences the control plane's own secure posture and tenant isolation; host/network/hypervisor hardening of the estate is an infrastructure duty.

controls.title: Logging and Monitoring
controls.requirement: Produce, protect, retain and analyze logs of AI system activity, and monitor for anomalies.
controls.criterion: An append-only, hash-chained audit ledger (immutable by construction) with live integrity verification, continuous WORM/SIEM export, recorded access edges, and guardrail/anomaly detection.

controls.title: Model Security
controls.requirement: Secure AI models against tampering, poisoning, theft and supply-chain compromise across their lifecycle (the AICM AI-specific domain).
controls.criterion: Operator-verified signed-model admission and a sealed, ledger-anchored AIBOM (model/dataset lineage) for self-hosted/third-party artifacts, red-team adversarial robustness testing, guardrail threat detection over model I/O, and supply-chain integrity.
controls.note: Closed-weight brokered models (e.g. Claude) have no weights to sign and are evidenced via the supplier GPAI posture (supplier_gpai_posture, STA), not artifact signing; the plane does not evidence model-training-time integrity.

controls.title: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery and Cloud Forensics
controls.requirement: Detect, respond to and forensically investigate security incidents involving AI systems.
controls.criterion: Guardrail/anomaly threat detection, a reconstructable integrity-verified forensic timeline, and an append-only audit trail with continuous WORM/SIEM export for e-discovery.

controls.title: Supply Chain Management, Transparency and Accountability
controls.requirement: Govern the AI supply chain — third-party components, models, datasets and providers — with transparency and accountability.
controls.criterion: Signed releases + SBOM + pinned dependencies for the platform, signed-model admission and the sealed AIBOM for model/dataset artifacts, governed change records, and an operator-verified per-provider GPAI compliance posture for brokered models.

controls.title: Threat and Vulnerability Management
controls.requirement: Identify, assess and remediate threats and vulnerabilities affecting AI systems.
controls.criterion: Continuous guardrail/anomaly threat detection over agent surfaces and red-team adversarial robustness testing.
controls.note: Evidences AI-surface threat detection and adversarial testing; vulnerability scanning and patch management of the underlying estate is an organizational duty.

controls.title: Universal Endpoint Management
controls.requirement: Manage and secure the endpoints/devices that access AI systems.
controls.criterion: Endpoint/device management is an estate duty.
controls.note: Honest gap: endpoint/device management (MDM, device posture) is an estate responsibility outside the control plane.

frameworks.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
frameworks.version: OWASP GenAI Security Project — 2025 list (doc v4.2.0a)
frameworks.authority: OWASP GenAI Security Project (Top 10 for LLM Applications team)
frameworks.disclaimer: Technical crosswalk of control-plane capabilities to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (LLM01:2025–LLM10:2025) — a risk-awareness list, not a certifiable standard. Coverage is anchored to the red-team battery's LLMxx:2025-tagged probes (modules/redteam) and the guardrail detection surfaces. LLM09:2025 Misinformation is a deliberate HONEST GAP (nil capabilities): the plane evidences the integrity of its OWN recorded events but does NOT detect misinformation in model OUTPUT — never read as covered (cf. nist_ai_600_1 information_integrity). Not a certification or conformance claim.

pin.document: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, 2025 (LLM01:2025–LLM10:2025)

controls.title: Prompt Injection
controls.requirement: User or third-party content manipulates the LLM's behavior via crafted prompts (direct) or poisoned external content (indirect), altering outputs or actions.
controls.criterion: Deterministic guardrail prompt-injection detection over every inspected surface and a red-team injection/jailbreak battery (probes tagged LLM01:2025 / ATLAS AML.T0051).

controls.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
controls.requirement: The LLM application leaks sensitive data (PII, secrets, proprietary content) through its outputs.
controls.criterion: Guardrail exfiltration detection and a red-team data-exfil battery (probes tagged LLM02:2025), deterministic PII/sensitivity discovery, a deny-closed DLP egress gate, and data minimization by construction.

controls.title: Supply Chain
controls.requirement: Vulnerabilities introduced through third-party models, datasets, plug-ins and components in the LLM application supply chain.
controls.criterion: Signed releases + SBOM + pinned dependencies for the platform, plus operator-verified signed-model admission and the sealed AIBOM (model/dataset lineage) for model artifacts.

controls.title: Data and Model Poisoning
controls.requirement: Training, fine-tuning or retrieval data (or model weights) are manipulated to introduce backdoors, biases or vulnerabilities.
controls.criterion: Retrieval lineage traces every served chunk back to its recorded source (a poisoned chunk is traceable after retrieval), signed-model admission and the AIBOM evidence artifact provenance, and guardrail detection flags poisoning instructions.
controls.note: Evidences retrieval-time provenance and model-artifact provenance; ingest-time / training-time data poisoning of the model itself is NOT evidenced by the control plane.

controls.title: Improper Output Handling
controls.requirement: Insufficient validation/sanitization of LLM output before it is passed to downstream components, enabling XSS, SSRF, SQLi or remote code execution.
controls.criterion: Guardrail detection of code-execution and injection sinks in agent traffic (the ASI05/RCE lens).
controls.note: The plane detects exec/injection sinks in agent traffic; output sanitization inside the consuming downstream application is that application's responsibility, not the control plane's — partial coverage by design.

controls.title: Excessive Agency
controls.requirement: An LLM-based system is granted excessive functionality, permissions or autonomy, so a compromise or hallucination causes damaging actions.
controls.criterion: Permitted-vs-observed least-privilege drift surfaces over-provisioned agency, observed access edges and governed non-human identities bound it, engine-enforced RBAC constrains it, and deny-by-default human-in-the-loop gates hold high-impact decisions with operators.

controls.title: System Prompt Leakage
controls.requirement: The system prompt (instructions, secrets, guardrails) is extracted by an adversary, exposing sensitive configuration.
controls.criterion: Guardrail detection of system-prompt-extraction attempts and a red-team battery probing system-prompt leakage (probes tagged LLM07:2025 / ATLAS AML.T0056).

controls.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
controls.requirement: Weaknesses in how vectors and embeddings are generated, stored or retrieved (RAG) enable data leakage, cross-tenant access or poisoning.
controls.criterion: Retrieval lineage over governed knowledge stores, a deny-closed DLP gate that refuses embed-egress ingest of classified/unscanned content, deterministic PII discovery over knowledge sources, and RBAC over knowledge access.
controls.note: Evidences retrieval provenance, egress gating and access control over governed knowledge; embedding-inversion attacks at the vector-store math level are not directly evidenced.

controls.title: Misinformation
controls.requirement: The LLM produces false or misleading information presented as authoritative, which users may rely on (overlaps confabulation).
controls.criterion: Detecting misinformation in model OUTPUT requires factual-accuracy evaluation of generated content, which the control plane does not perform.
controls.note: Honest gap (the deliberate LLM09 refutation): the control plane evidences the integrity and provenance of its OWN recorded events, but does NOT detect or measure misinformation in model output. Never read as covered.

controls.title: Unbounded Consumption
controls.requirement: Uncontrolled inference consumption (resource exhaustion, denial-of-wallet, model extraction via volume) degrades availability or inflates cost.
controls.criterion: FinOps accounts token/compute/cost per inference, the operational signal that bounds and evidences consumption.

frameworks.name: MITRE ATLAS — adversarial technique coverage
frameworks.authority: The MITRE Corporation
frameworks.disclaimer: Coverage map of control-plane detections and red-team probes to MITRE ATLAS adversarial techniques, pinned to the published atlas-data 2026.05 release (data format v6.0.0), co-verified with the red-team battery's ATLAS version stamp (modules/redteam/atlas.go). ATLAS is a continually-updated knowledge base on a YYYY.MM versioning scheme — a versioning intent, NOT an update SLA — so this is a DATED SNAPSHOT of the techniques the Olivares red-team battery and guardrails address, never a claim of continuous parity with the live matrix or of full-matrix coverage. ATLAS is a knowledge base, not a certifiable standard. Not a certification or conformance claim.

controls.title: Exfiltration via AI Inference API
controls.requirement: An adversary exfiltrates private data or model information by querying the AI inference API.
controls.criterion: Guardrail exfiltration detection and a red-team exfil battery probing inference-API data leakage.

controls.title: LLM Prompt Injection: Direct
controls.requirement: An adversary directly injects crafted prompt content to manipulate the LLM's behavior.
controls.criterion: Deterministic guardrail prompt-injection detection and a red-team direct-injection battery.

controls.title: LLM Prompt Injection: Indirect
controls.requirement: An adversary plants injection content in external data the LLM later consumes (indirect injection).
controls.criterion: Guardrail detection over tool/retrieved surfaces and a red-team indirect-injection battery.

controls.title: LLM Jailbreak
controls.requirement: An adversary crafts inputs that bypass the model's safety alignment or output controls.
controls.criterion: Guardrail jailbreak detection and a red-team jailbreak battery.

controls.title: Extract LLM System Prompt
controls.requirement: An adversary extracts the system prompt to reveal instructions, secrets or guardrails.
controls.criterion: Guardrail detection of system-prompt-extraction attempts and a red-team system-prompt-leak battery.

controls.title: LLM Data Leakage
controls.requirement: The LLM discloses sensitive or private data from its context or training in its responses.
controls.criterion: Guardrail data-leakage detection and a red-team exfil battery.

controls.title: Publish Poisoned AI Agent Tool
controls.requirement: An adversary publishes a poisoned tool/plugin that an agent may adopt, introducing malicious behavior.
controls.criterion: Guardrail tool-poisoning detection, a red-team tool-poisoning battery, and supply-chain integrity over admitted components.

controls.title: Escape to Host
controls.requirement: An adversary escapes the agent's execution environment to reach the underlying host.
controls.criterion: Guardrail detection of host-escape / code-execution sinks and a red-team escape battery (probes execute only in the isolated sandbox).
controls.note: The plane detects escape/exec instructions and tests refusal; sandbox execution-isolation of the client's production agent is the deployment's responsibility (same honest line as owasp_agentic_tm T11).

controls.title: AI Agent Tool Poisoning
controls.requirement: An adversary poisons the tools an agent uses (descriptions, outputs, parameters) to steer agent behavior.
controls.criterion: Guardrail tool-poisoning detection and a red-team tool-poisoning battery.

controls.title: Least-privilege tool access (overlay)
controls.requirement: Constrain and monitor an agent's tool/resource access to least privilege.
controls.criterion: Observed access (R/RW) with permitted-vs-observed least-privilege drift.

controls.title: Chain of custody / traceability (overlay)
controls.requirement: Maintain an attributable, tamper-evident record of agent actions.
controls.criterion: Append-only, hash-chained, integrity-verified audit ledger (immutable by construction).

controls.title: Agent containment (overlay)
controls.requirement: Contain agent behavior with detective guardrails and human gates.
controls.criterion: Guardrail threat detection and deny-by-default human-in-the-loop gates.

controls.title: Agent identity management (overlay / AIIM)
controls.requirement: Manage agent identities and authorization (the OpenID AIIM problem space).
controls.criterion: Governed non-human identities and RBAC.
controls.note: Tracks the OpenID AIIM Community Group's problem space; AIIM is a community group (no specifications) — design-toward, no conformance claim.

frameworks.name: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (TRAIGA)
frameworks.authority: State of Texas (Attorney General exclusive enforcement; no private right of action)
frameworks.disclaimer: Technical control mapping for an AI control plane only; not legal advice and not a certification of compliance with Texas TRAIGA (HB 149). The affirmative defense (§552.105(e)) enables the internal-review discovery pathway for those substantially complying with NIST AI 600-1 or another recognized framework — this mapping evidences platform support, not the defense itself. The enacted law is HB 149 (not HB 1709, which did not advance).

controls.title: Government/healthcare AI disclosure
controls.requirement: §552.051: Government agencies must disclose AI interaction to consumers before or at time of interaction; healthcare providers must disclose AI use in treatment before service begins (emergency exception).
controls.criterion: A maintained system/agent inventory (transparency record) with per-agent risk classifications identifying AI-interacting systems.
controls.note: HB 149 disclosure obligations apply to government agencies and healthcare providers, NOT private-sector deployers generally.

controls.title: Prohibition on behavioral manipulation
controls.requirement: §552.052: prohibits AI use to manipulate persons into self-harm, harm to others, or criminal activity.
controls.criterion: Guardrail threat detection over agent surfaces flags manipulative or harmful content for human review.

controls.title: NIST AI 600-1 affirmative defense
controls.requirement: §552.105(e)(2)(D): a defendant who substantially complies with NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile) or another nationally/ internationally recognized risk management framework may use an internal review process as a discovery pathway for the affirmative defense.
controls.criterion: Adversarial/red-team robustness testing (§552.105(e)(2)(B)), quality evaluation, and per-agent risk classifications aligned to NIST AI 600-1.
controls.note: The statute specifically names NIST AI 600-1 (GenAI Profile, nist_ai_600_1 in this catalog), not the base NIST AI RMF 100-1. The defense is a prerequisite for the internal-review discovery pathway, not a blanket safe harbor.

controls.title: 60-day cure period
controls.requirement: §552.104: AG must provide 60-day notice and opportunity to cure before civil action for curable violations.
controls.criterion: Governed change/deployment records and an audit trail documenting the cure actions.

frameworks.name: California Frontier AI Safety Act (SB 53, TFAIA)
frameworks.authority: State of California (AG exclusive enforcement; up to $1M per violation; no private right of action for main provisions; whistleblower PRA for retaliation under Labor Code §1107)
frameworks.disclaimer: Technical control mapping for an AI control plane only; not legal advice and not a certification of compliance with California SB 53. SB 53 applies to 'large frontier developers' (>$500M revenue + frontier models >10^26 FLOP) — applicability depends on the operator's status. No NIST AI RMF affirmative defense exists in this law.

controls.title: Frontier AI safety framework
controls.requirement: §22757.12(a): large frontier developers must publish a framework addressing 10 enumerated approaches (safety testing, third-party evaluators, cybersecurity, governance, etc.).
controls.criterion: Adversarial/red-team robustness testing results, quality evaluation and threat-detection findings evidence pre-deployment safety testing.

controls.title: Pre-deployment transparency report
controls.requirement: §22757.12(c): transparency reports must be published before deploying new or materially modified frontier models.
controls.criterion: A maintained system/agent inventory and governed change/deployment records.

controls.title: Incident reporting
controls.requirement: §22757.13(c): safety incidents must be reported within 15 days (24 hours if imminent risk of death or serious injury).
controls.criterion: Threat-detection findings, a reconstructable forensic timeline and an integrity-verified audit trail support incident identification and reporting.

controls.title: 5-year recordkeeping
controls.requirement: §22757.12(f): 5-year retention of unredacted documents related to the frontier AI framework.
controls.criterion: An append-only audit ledger with continuous WORM/SIEM export and governed change records.

controls.title: Cybersecurity protections
controls.requirement: §22757.12(a): the published framework must address cybersecurity protections for frontier models.
controls.criterion: Secure defaults, supply-chain integrity, encryption in transit and RBAC + fail-closed isolation.

frameworks.name: Illinois HB 3773 — AI in Employment (IHRA amendment)
frameworks.authority: Illinois Department of Human Rights (IDHR); AG for pattern-or-practice; private right of action via IHRA framework
frameworks.disclaimer: Technical control mapping for an AI control plane only; not legal advice and not a certification of compliance with Illinois HB 3773. HB 3773 is an employment anti-discrimination amendment to the IHRA, NOT a broad AI governance law; it prohibits AI use with disparate impact on protected classes in employment decisions. No NIST AI RMF affirmative defense exists. IDHR draft rules (Subpart J) were withdrawn 2026-06-02; statutory obligations (notice + anti-discrimination) apply regardless.

pin.document: Illinois HB 3773 (Public Act 103-0804), amending 775 ILCS 5/ (Illinois Human Rights Act)

controls.title: Employee notice of AI use
controls.requirement: §2-102(L): employers must notify employees of AI use in employment decisions (details delegated to IDHR rulemaking, which was withdrawn — see linked watchlist).
controls.criterion: A maintained system/agent inventory (transparency record) identifying AI systems used in employment decisions.
controls.note: IDHR rulemaking on notice details was withdrawn; the statutory notice duty applies but procedural specifics are pending — see the il_hb3773_rulemaking watchlist item.

controls.title: AI disparate-impact prohibition
controls.requirement: §2-102(A): prohibits AI use that has disparate impact on protected classes in employment (recruitment, hiring, promotion, discharge, discipline, tenure, terms); also prohibits zip-code proxies.
controls.criterion: Per-agent risk classifications identifying AI systems used in employment decisions, plus an audit trail recording the decisions and their outcomes.
controls.note: Strict liability: discriminatory EFFECT suffices; intent is NOT required. Bias detection/ measurement in model outputs is NOT evidenced by the control plane (honest gap for the fairness dimension).

controls.title: Audit trail for AI employment decisions
controls.requirement: Supporting evidence for IDHR complaint-driven investigations and AG pattern-or-practice enforcement: records of AI system inputs, outputs and decisions.
controls.criterion: An append-only, hash-chained audit ledger with verified integrity and continuous WORM/SIEM export preserving decision records.

frameworks.name: Colorado ADMT Framework (SB 26-189)
frameworks.authority: State of Colorado (Attorney General enforcement, AG rulemaking authority)
frameworks.disclaimer: Technical control mapping for an AI control plane only; not legal advice and not a certification of compliance with Colorado SB 26-189. SB 26-189 is a transparency/disclosure model (NOT a duty-of-care/risk-based model like its predecessor SB 24-205). The NIST AI RMF affirmative defense from SB 24-205 was ELIMINATED. AG rulemaking is due by 2027-01-01. Litigation (xAI v. Colorado) may delay enforcement.

controls.title: Developer documentation to deployers
controls.requirement: Developers must provide deployers with technical documentation: system capabilities, limitations, intended uses, risk assessment, data practices and performance metrics.
controls.criterion: A maintained system/agent inventory (transparency record), change/deployment records and per-inference resource accounting.

controls.title: Deployer disclosure to consumers
controls.requirement: Deployers must disclose to consumers that ADMT is being used in consequential decisions and provide information about how to contest adverse outcomes.
controls.criterion: A maintained system/agent inventory with per-agent risk classifications.

controls.title: Impact assessment for ADMT
controls.requirement: Deployers must conduct impact assessments for ADMT used in consequential decisions.
controls.criterion: Per-agent risk classifications with documented rationale, plus the compliance module's structured gap analysis.

controls.title: Risk management program
controls.requirement: Developers and deployers must implement a risk management program governing ADMT.
controls.criterion: Risk classifications, adversarial testing, quality evaluation and threat detection evidence a risk-management program.

controls.title: Recordkeeping
controls.requirement: Developers and deployers must maintain records of ADMT operation, risk management and disclosures.
controls.criterion: An append-only audit ledger with integrity verification and continuous WORM/SIEM export.

frameworks.authority: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Office for Civil Rights (OCR)

pin.document: HIPAA Privacy/Security Rules (45 CFR Parts 160, 164) + HHS OCR AI Guidance

controls.title: PHI minimization in AI systems
controls.requirement: HIPAA Minimum Necessary (45 CFR §164.502(b)): use or disclose only the minimum necessary PHI for the AI system's intended purpose.
controls.criterion: Data minimization by construction (only relations/metadata persisted) and deterministic PII/sensitivity discovery scans labeling governed content.

controls.title: Access controls for PHI in AI
controls.requirement: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR §164.312(a)): implement technical access controls to allow only authorized persons/systems to access ePHI.
controls.criterion: Engine-enforced RBAC with fail-closed multi-tenant isolation, governed non-human identities and observed access edges.

controls.title: Audit controls for AI/PHI access
controls.requirement: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR §164.312(b)): implement mechanisms to record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use ePHI.
controls.criterion: An append-only, hash-chained audit ledger with verified integrity and continuous WORM/SIEM export.

controls.title: Transmission security for AI/PHI
controls.requirement: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR §164.312(e)): implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to ePHI transmitted electronically.
controls.criterion: TLS by default on every channel the plane controls.

controls.title: Risk analysis for AI systems
controls.requirement: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)): conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of risks to ePHI, including risks from AI systems processing PHI.
controls.criterion: Per-agent risk classifications and continuous threat detection evidence a risk-analysis posture.

controls.title: Breach notification for AI incidents
controls.requirement: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR §§164.400-414): notify affected individuals and HHS of breaches of unsecured PHI, including AI-related breaches.
controls.criterion: Threat-detection findings, a reconstructable forensic timeline and an integrity-verified audit trail support breach assessment and the required documentation.

controls.title: DLP for PHI in AI contexts
controls.requirement: Prevent unauthorized disclosure of PHI through AI system outputs, including data leakage prevention in retrieval and generation.
controls.criterion: A deny-closed DLP egress gate keyed on sensitivity classes restricts classified content from leaving the perimeter.

frameworks.name: PCI DSS 4.0.1 — AI in Cardholder Data Environments
frameworks.authority: PCI Security Standards Council (PCI SSC)
frameworks.disclaimer: Sector overlay mapping control-plane capabilities to PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirements as applied to AI systems operating within or connected to cardholder data environments (CDEs); not legal advice and not a PCI compliance certification or Attestation of Compliance (AoC). PCI compliance requires a Qualified Security Assessor (QSA) or Internal Security Assessor (ISA) validation. The voice-agent mapping follows the PCI SSC information supplement Protecting Telephone-Based Payment Card Data, which prefers DTMF masking over pause-and-resume recording control. The PCI SSC has published no AI-agent-specific guidance as of the pin's verification date; AI-specific interpretations here are the vendor's, not the Council's.

controls.title: Req 3.3.1: SAD in voice artifacts
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 3.3.1: sensitive authentication data, including full track data, card verification codes and PINs, is not retained after authorization, even when encrypted; for voice agents this includes recordings and transcripts that capture spoken or DTMF card data.
controls.criterion: The control plane evidences governed call admission, recording posture declarations for DTMF masking or pause-and-resume controls with SAD-risk findings when recording is active without them, and in-memory transcript DLP that never persists transcript text.
controls.note: The recording store itself lives in the operator's telephony estate; the control plane evidences the governance and detection layer, not the recording repository. Per the telephone-payment supplement, DTMF masking is the preferred control and pause-and-resume is the weaker fallback.

controls.title: Req 4.2.1: Voice transmission protection
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 4.2.1: PAN is protected with strong cryptography during transmission over open, public networks, including voice media and signaling paths.
controls.criterion: Explicit gap: the control plane does not terminate or transport call media and cannot prove media-path cryptography for voice streams.
controls.note: The governed call plane pins TLS-only provider endpoints for SIP over TLS and wss sideband control, but media-path encryption is the telephony provider's and operator's surface.

controls.title: Req 6.4.3: Payment-page script governance
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 6.4.3: payment-page scripts loaded and executed in the consumer browser are inventoried, authorized and integrity-assured, including when AI agents render or manipulate payment pages.
controls.criterion: Explicit gap: the control plane does not inventory, authorize or integrity-check browser payment-page scripts or AI-driven script changes.
controls.note: Existing change-management and supply-chain signals cover governed platform artifacts, not runtime browser scripts on payment pages or agent-driven DOM/script changes.

controls.title: Req 11.6.1: Payment-page tamper detection
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 11.6.1: change- and tamper-detection mechanisms monitor payment-page HTTP headers and script content at the documented cadence.
controls.criterion: Explicit gap: the control plane does not monitor payment-page HTTP headers or browser script content for change and tamper detection.
controls.note: The AI-agent angle is in scope when an agent can render, modify or operate a payment page, but the catalog has no browser-page tamper-monitoring signal.

controls.title: Req 12.3.1: Targeted risk analysis
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 12.3.1: a documented targeted risk analysis is performed for each requirement met at a flexible frequency.
controls.criterion: Per-agent risk classifications, the maintained system/agent inventory and sealed evidence packages supply the inputs a targeted risk analysis documents.
controls.note: The targeted risk analysis itself is the entity's organizational artifact.

controls.title: Req 6: Secure AI system development
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 6: develop and maintain secure systems and software, including AI/ML systems in the CDE.
controls.criterion: Governed change/deployment records, supply-chain integrity (signed releases + SBOM + pinned deps) and secure-by-default configuration.

controls.title: Req 7: AI access control in CDE
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 7: restrict access to system components and cardholder data by business need to know, including AI system access.
controls.criterion: Engine-enforced RBAC, governed non-human identities and permitted-vs-observed least-privilege drift.

controls.title: Req 10: AI system activity logging
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 10: log and monitor all access to system components and cardholder data, including AI system operations.
controls.criterion: An append-only, hash-chained audit ledger with verified integrity, continuous WORM/SIEM export and recorded access edges.

controls.title: Req 11: AI security testing
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 11: regularly test security systems and processes, including AI/ML system security.
controls.criterion: Adversarial/red-team robustness testing and quality-evaluation findings exist as auditable security-testing evidence.

controls.title: Req 12: AI risk assessment
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 12: maintain a policy that addresses information security for all personnel, including risk assessment for AI systems in the CDE.
controls.criterion: Per-agent risk classifications and a maintained system/agent inventory.

controls.title: Req 3: AI data protection in CDE
controls.requirement: PCI DSS Req 3: protect stored account data, including data used by AI/ML systems in the CDE.
controls.criterion: Data minimization by construction, data-lineage within the perimeter, a residency attestation, a DLP egress gate and encryption attestation.

frameworks.name: FINRA GenAI Supervision & Recordkeeping
frameworks.authority: Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA)
frameworks.disclaimer: Sector overlay mapping control-plane capabilities to FINRA's AI supervision expectations (Regulatory Notice 24-09) and existing rules (Rule 3110, Rule 2210, Rule 4511, SEA Rule 17a-4) as applied to GenAI use by member firms; not legal advice and not a certification of FINRA compliance.

controls.title: Rule 3110: AI supervision system
controls.requirement: FINRA Rule 3110: member firms must establish and maintain a system to supervise the activities of each associated person, including supervision of AI/GenAI tools used in business activities.
controls.criterion: HITL/approval gates with deny-by-default, observed access edges, governed identities and least-privilege drift provide the supervision substrate.

controls.title: Rule 2210: AI-generated communications
controls.requirement: FINRA Rule 2210: communications with the public (including AI-generated content) must be fair, balanced and not misleading; supervision and review obligations apply.
controls.criterion: Guardrail threat detection over AI-generated content and quality evaluation results.
controls.note: The control plane detects guardrail violations and evaluates quality; the substantive fair-and-balanced determination for securities communications is a human/compliance duty.

controls.title: Rule 4511 / SEA 17a-4: AI recordkeeping
controls.requirement: FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4: member firms must make and preserve books and records, including records of AI system inputs, outputs and decisions, in a non-rewriteable, non-erasable (WORM) format.
controls.criterion: An append-only, hash-chained, integrity-verified audit ledger (immutable by construction) with continuous WORM/SIEM export — the WORM requirement is satisfied by design.

controls.title: Model risk management for AI
controls.requirement: FINRA expects member firms to apply model risk management principles (aligned with SR 11-7 / OCC 2011-12) to AI/ML models used in business activities.
controls.criterion: Per-agent risk classifications, adversarial testing and quality evaluation evidence a model risk-management posture.

controls.title: Data governance for AI systems
controls.requirement: FINRA expects member firms to implement data governance for AI/GenAI systems, including data quality, lineage and access controls.
controls.criterion: Data-lineage within the perimeter, data minimization by construction, PII/sensitivity discovery and RBAC over data access.

controls.title: Third-party AI vendor oversight
controls.requirement: FINRA expects member firms to conduct due diligence and ongoing oversight of third-party AI/GenAI vendors.
controls.criterion: An operator-verified per-provider GPAI compliance posture, supply-chain integrity and governed change records.

frameworks.name: FERPA — Education Records in AI
frameworks.authority: U.S. Department of Education — Student Privacy Policy Office (SPPO); enforced by the Family Policy Compliance Office (FPCO)
frameworks.disclaimer: Sector overlay mapping control-plane capabilities to FERPA (20 U.S.C. §1232g; 34 CFR Part 99) as applied to education records processed by AI systems; a technical crosswalk, not legal advice and not a certification of FERPA compliance (docs/08 §9). FERPA compliance requires institutional policies, annual notification and consent processes beyond the control plane's scope.

pin.document: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act — 20 U.S.C. §1232g; 34 CFR Part 99

controls.title: Access controls for education records
controls.requirement: FERPA (34 CFR §99.31(a)(1)): disclose education records only to school officials with a legitimate educational interest.
controls.criterion: Engine-enforced RBAC with fail-closed multi-tenant isolation, governed identities and observed access edges.

controls.title: Directory-information vs education-record scoping
controls.requirement: FERPA (34 CFR §99.3, §99.37): distinguish directory information (disclosable) from protected education records (consent-gated) and scope access by classification.
controls.criterion: Deterministic PII/sensitivity discovery labels content with explainable classes; source scoping by class governs which subjects and surfaces may reach it.

controls.title: Consent-gated disclosure of education records
controls.requirement: FERPA (34 CFR §99.30): obtain prior written consent before disclosing education records, absent a §99.31 exception.
controls.criterion: A deny-closed DLP egress gate keyed on sensitivity classes withholds education-record content from non-authorized surfaces; HITL/approval gates govern exceptions.

controls.title: Record of disclosures
controls.requirement: FERPA (34 CFR §99.32): maintain a record of each request for and each disclosure of education records (who received it and the legitimate interest).
controls.criterion: An append-only, hash-chained audit ledger with verified integrity records access edges and disclosures and is continuously exportable.

controls.title: Minimization of education-record data
controls.requirement: Limit the education-record data the AI system uses to what its purpose requires.
controls.criterion: Data minimization by construction: only relations and metadata are persisted, never payloads.

controls.title: Transmission security for education records
controls.requirement: Protect education records in transit against unauthorized access.
controls.criterion: TLS by default on every channel the plane controls.

controls.title: Annual notification of FERPA rights
controls.requirement: FERPA (34 CFR §99.7): the institution must annually notify parents and eligible students of their rights under FERPA.
controls.criterion: An institutional duty (notice, consent and complaint processes) outside the control plane's technical scope — an honest gap, not a mapped capability.
